## 1. What this block is, in one sentence

**This is the block in which the date at the foot of the sheet comes and goes and nothing is shut, and somebody stands in the doorway of the low room at the back of the office at the low end of that market street and does not go in, and the finding is that a man behind a counter who was born in that street is the cheapest instrument an occupation has and nobody in nine counties has ever asked him what a gate is for, and the year turns on a market morning for the first time in this manuscript's memory, and a woman of about twenty-nine is asked for something by somebody in her own trade and says no, and the close is that about four hundred places are now writing a paper and no two copies agree, and that a paper nobody can seal binds nobody, which is safe, and that a county which can only refuse cannot hold, which is not.** It is also the block that spends one of the four names left in the volume's budget, that carries the year turn, that prints no System panel, and that leaves the drawer in that low room shut and the seal still in it.

`outline/volume-17.md` §8 Block 2 and §9 and §10 and §11 and §12 and §15 and §16 are binding and are not softened by anything in this file. `outline/series.md`'s Volume 17 row is fixed. `outline/ending.md` is fixed. **DO NOT MOVE THE ENDING. DO NOT INTRODUCE A NEW FINAL ENEMY. THE ANTAGONIST IS THE SAME MAN HE HAS BEEN FOR SIXTEEN VOLUMES AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS VOLUME PUTS HIM IN A ROOM.**

## 4. What the block must contain

**THE SHEET'S DATE COMES AND GOES AND SHUTS NOTHING, AND THE PAGE SAYS SO IN THE HOUSE'S CENSUS FORM.** At Chapter 0813 there are five days left in it and about four people in that market street have worked out inside nine seconds that five days is a working week, and five have not. **At Chapter 0814 the date is two days past and nothing in nine counties is shut and about nine hundred people along eleven miles of made road never knew there was a date on it at all.** **Do not print the date as more than two days past at Chapter 0814 and do not print it as more than five days off at Chapter 0813.** The fourth line of that roll is still empty on all three copies at the block's last dateline and the roll is one hundred and eighty-five days on the frame at the first dateline and two hundred and twenty-seven at the last, and it is not filled in and not taken down and not torn up, and **the new sheet stays nailed up beside the roll and not over it, and the count of things on that frame is still five and the count of questions on it is still three.**

**THE DOORWAY IS NOT GONE THROUGH, AND THE PERSON WHO STANDS IN IT IS NOT THE PROTAGONIST.** At about the tenth hour of one of this block's datelines, a person stands in the doorway of the low room at the back of the office at the low end of that market street and does not go in, and about nine people are in that street and about four of them see him stand there and about five do not. **He goes away and the door is shut behind him and nobody followed him and nobody asked him why he had come, and nobody in nine counties asked what a seal is for, and the drawer eleven inches deep in that room was not opened, and the county's one seal and its ribbon and a set of standard weights are still in it.** **THE PROTAGONIST IS NOT IN THAT DOORWAY AND IS NOT AT THAT DOOR AND IS NOT ASKED WHAT A SEAL IS FOR, AND A SUCCESSOR MAY NOT PUT HIM AT IT IN BLOCK 0003 EITHER.**

**THE FINDING IS ON THE PAGE AND IT IS ABOUT A MAN BEHIND A COUNTER AND IT IS NOT A VERDICT ON HIM.** A man behind the counter at the front of that office was born in that street and is about the age he has always been and nobody in nine counties has asked him anything, and about four people in nine counties have said that a counter and a door and a man who was born in the street is the cheapest instrument an occupation has, being that it needs nobody to travel and nobody to be paid and nobody to agree, and five have said that about the cheapest instrument is also the one nobody in nine counties has looked at, **and neither of those two things is printed anywhere but the narration and neither of them goes in any document.**

**THE COST IS THE REFUSAL AND IT IS IN HER OWN TRADE AND SHE SAYS NO.** Somebody in the woman of about twenty-nine's own trade asks her for something she does not give him. **The fourth ruled head in that room is still empty at every one of the ten datelines and no fifth head is ruled on any of them, and the register still holds ten questions with no finding under any of them, and the day-book still stands at eleven entries on all ten datelines, and the copyist of about twenty-six rules no head and is told about none of it.** **Nothing about the practice, the ten things, the four lines of chalk, the three answers of Batch 0001, the sheet, the hand paper, the seal or the bleed goes into any document in this volume.**

**THE TURN IS THE YEAR TURNING ON A MARKET MORNING.** Day 3036 is a Saturday, and the year turns at the first of Thawmonth YR 324 on a market morning with the room over the weigh-house open and the practice not running, **and the page says that is the twenty-fifth first of a month in a row and that a year turns on a market morning for the first time in this manuscript's memory, and about four people in that market street had worked out inside nine seconds what a year is and five had not.** The first of Thawmonth comes to those boards and finds five things on them and nothing standing at them, **and it is the second and last month boundary inside this block, being the only one.**

**THE CLOSE IS THAT NO TWO COPIES AGREE AND THAT A PAPER NOBODY CAN SEAL BINDS NOBODY, WHICH IS SAFE, AND THAT A COUNTY WHICH CAN ONLY REFUSE CANNOT HOLD, WHICH IS NOT.** At the block's last dateline, about four hundred places are writing a paper by hand because nobody has a seal to give them, **this county's copy has nine lines with a trade on each and no name on any and no seal, and nobody in nine counties has been asked whose trade is on any of its nine lines, and nobody in nine counties knows who else has a copy, and the page says that no two of about four hundred copies agree with one another because nobody has asked them to.** The finding is stated once, plainly, and it is not resolved, and **neither half of it is a rescue and neither is a plan.**

**THE NAME BUDGET FOR VOLUME 17 IS TWO SPENT AND FOUR HELD AFTER BATCH 0001, BEING `Nell Thrush` AND `Ninian Crowe`.** `Aren Kest`, `Mara Vey`, `Tovan Kest`, `Sera Quen`, `Hester Vane`, `Orme Skell`, `Dav Rundle`, `Tarr Lyster`, `Corve Sallow`, `Renn Ottery`, `Pell Arkwright`, `Wyn Fell`, `Abel Chinn`, `Brida Lenth` and `Bessie Dellow` are returns and cost nothing. **`Sabra Rolf` and `Gallow` may not be used for a new first name, and neither may `Iven` and `Marrow`, and neither may `Renn` or `Ost` as a surname, and neither may any first name or surname already printed anywhere in the manuscript.** `Corryn Falder`, `Tosh Sennen`, `Dalla Quillan` and `Prue Sillick` were checked against all eight hundred and ten files and print nowhere, and `Osmund`, `Halla` and `Ivo` were checked and are already printed in Volumes 05, 09 and 10 and may not be used.

A NAME IS NOT A PROMOTION AND A NAMED PERSON IS NOT A LEADER AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BLOCK GIVES THE NAME AN OFFICE, A RULE, A VOTE, OR A SENTENCE IN FRONT OF ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED PEOPLE.**

**THE RELATIONSHIP WORK IS NOT DONE HERE AND THE HOUSE SAYS SO ON THE PAGE.** `outline/series.md`'s Volume 17 relationship work is separating the symbol from the partner, and §8 Block 2 does not do it. **So: nothing about the two of them is in any document, the word is not printed, nobody comments, nobody was thanked, the four and a half years are never described as four and a half years about the two of them, and no chapter of this block ends on the two of them.** At most this block puts the second lamp at the foot of those thirteen stairs on the page in the house way, being that it is lit at the fourth hour on the five mornings this block carries on which the room is shut, and **it is not carried down any stair and it is not put in the middle of anybody's work, because Block 0003 spends that and the block that spends it must be the block that does it.** The legal form stays deferred to Volume 18.

**THE COST OF THE BLOCK IS ON THE PAGE AND IS NOT CURED IN IT.** The leg, which takes eleven miles in four hours before light and about nine otherwise and is worse than it was at the close of Volume 16; the ear on the side the stick is on, which is permanent and is the side she spoke from and which he turns his head away from on purpose; the standing fact that he cannot be near the works without somebody standing with him; **and the bleed, which is ninety-three days old on this block's first dateline and one hundred and thirty-four on its last and has not faded by anything anybody has done to it, which nobody in nine counties has asked him about, which is in no document, which has never been said out loud in a room, and which gets no panel and no explanation and no panel-shaped paragraph in any of these ten files.** **The scar is four hundred and thirty-three days old at the block's first dateline and four hundred and seventy-four at its last and is not cured and is not going to close over.** The ninth yard of the wall has not been started and does not start in this block, and the mallet is not picked up, and the third course of sill at the culvert is unlaid, and the ninth thing is still shut by nine hurdles put there by the people at the end of it who would like them to stay.

**THE ONE SYSTEM PANEL IN THE WHOLE OF VOLUME 17 IS RESERVED FOR BLOCK 0003 AND IS NOT SPENT IN THIS BLOCK. These ten files print no panel and no panel-shaped paragraph, and a panel here is a panel spent on nothing.**

**THE ANTAGONIST'S NAME IS PRINTED ZERO TIMES IN THIS BLOCK AND ZERO TIMES IN THIS VOLUME AND IS NEVER TO BE PRINTED AGAIN IN THIS PROJECT.** Volume 16's two printings at `chapter-0781.md` and `chapter-0797.md` were both documents and both are spent. Refer to him and to his instrument as *that notice*, *the Marshal's hand*, *the sheet*, *the offer*, *the warrant* or *the people with the warrant*.

## 5. The ending of the block

**A completed beat, not a cliffhanger cut in the middle of a sentence.** The sheet is on the frame beside three copies of a roll and its date is twenty days past and the fourth line is empty on all three copies and the roll is not filled in and not taken down and not torn up. **This county's copy of the hand paper still has nine lines on it and a trade on each and no name on any and no seal on it, and nobody in nine counties has been asked whose trade is on any of them.** The four lines of chalk are under the hood where the rain does not reach and are still four and are still not writing. **The register holds ten questions and gains no entry, no fifth head is ruled, the fourth ruled head is empty, the day-book stands at eleven entries on all ten datelines, and the leaf at the back of it carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody.** **The low room at the back of that office is not entered in this block and the drawer in it is not opened and the seal is still in it, and nobody is asked what a seal is for.**

**`outline/volume-17.md` §16 item 6's three promises are CARRIED INTO BLOCK 0003 UNCONDUCTED AND NONE OF THEM IS BROKEN HERE:** no chapter of this block enters the Gatehouse or puts anybody on about nine hundred yards of a stair or shows what is on the far side of the ninth of the nine stones; no consent of any sealed community is obtained, asked for, received or inferred, and the half leaf stays face down and no head is filled or ruled; and the roll is not filled, no name goes against any road, no road is shut on the strength of any paper, none of the three copies is taken down or torn up, no hurdle is lifted, no bar is tried, nobody goes up that cart track, the ninth yard does not start, the mallet is not picked up, and the drawer at the back of that office is not opened.

**`state/continuity.md` 1812 and `state/open-threads.md` 771 carry one warning forward and a successor may not learn the opposite of it:** four lines on a sill are not the beginning of a cure, a page in a woman's hand is not a cure, a sentence in an unclaimed hand on a folded sheet is not a cure, **a bleed that has not faded in ninety-two days is not a cure, and ONE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-FOUR IS THIS BLOCK'S OWN FIGURE AT ITS LAST DATELINE AND IT IS THE SAME WARNING AND NOT A NEW ONE: the inherited warning prints the same clause at two hundred and sixty days, which is the volume's last page and not this block's, that figure is not withdrawn and is not superseded, and the two are the same claim at two datelines and a writer inherits both and quotes whichever belongs to the chapter he is on**, a closed path is not destroyed and that is not good news, a gate coming off its hinges about nine hundred yards of a stair away is not a victory and a gate that is still held is not a defeat, being the man who went and looked is a job and not an honour and nobody was told so and nobody wrote it down, **and a line with a trade on it is not a name and a paper nobody can seal is not a freedom and is not the same as a paper nobody has to obey and is not a plan.**

## 6. The prohibitions, in one list

**This list is additions to `state/open-threads.md` items 765 to 775, and to 764, 763, 762, 761, 760, 759, 758, 756, 755, 754, 752, 751, 750, 747, 743 and to every clause of 745 to 719 that is still true. It does not replace them.**

- **Do not print a System panel**, the volume's one being reserved for Block 0003. **And these ten files print no panel-shaped paragraph about the bleed either, and it is not bold and not alone and not spoken aloud and nobody else knows.**
- **Do not print the antagonist's name once, and do not print the bare surname as a printing, and do not use either withdrawn reference of the kind that names him. And do not print the word *Gatehouse* in a mouth.**
- **Do not spend more than one name out of the four held, and do not leave this block's name unspent by accident, and do not spend a name out of Volume 16's closed six.**
- **Do not fill the roll, put a name against any road, shut a road on the strength of any paper, take down any of the three copies, tear one up, or nail anything over the roll.**
- **Do not go into the low room at the back of that office, do not open the drawer in it, do not name what is in it beyond the county's one seal, its ribbon and a set of standard weights, and do not ask anybody what a seal is for or what a gate is for.**
- **Do not conduct any of the three hand-offs.** No hurdle is lifted and no bar is tried up that shut track, **and a successor may not make the roadkeeper the one who tries it either**, and nobody goes up that cart track a third time and nobody is shown standing behind all nine hurdles. **The sealed community sends nothing and is never asked, and nothing in this block implies where it is, and the four copied pages and the re-anchoring and the reading of them in her own trade belong to Block 0003 and may not be touched here.**
- **Do not enter the Gatehouse, do not put anybody on about nine hundred yards of a stair, and do not report anything out of it.** The occupation is a sheet on a board and about nine men with a warrant who are not in this county.
- **Do not open, close or cut any route, do not explain the mechanism, do not say what a roadmark is, do not look at the notebook's separate leaf that says a person, and do not have any character notice the warmth of the left palm.**
- **Do not look over the ninth of the nine stones, do not cross them, do not show what is on the far side of them, and do not treat the omission as an oversight.** The dead grass in the scar stops at the ninth of them.
- **Do not reopen either refusal of Volume 15, do not argue with either, do not soften either, do not ask either of the two men who gave them anything, and do not put the man of forty-one in a scene or ask him anything.** He says sixteen words in the whole of Volume 16 and is asked nothing here.
- **Do not turn the nine houses at Wethergill, the nine households on that mile of stone and orchard, or the nine who refused the roll into a body.** They are nine houses, nine households that voted, and nine people who said one thing each.
- **Do not ask anybody for an account of having said no, do not ask the roadkeeper or the woman of about twenty-nine about the broom straw, and do not ask anybody whether she wrote the sentence on the folded sheet.**
- **Do not give Volume 16's three answers or this volume's first three a second time, do not merge any of the six, do not resolve the incompatibility between any of them, and do not let the protagonist be the author, the announcer, the summariser or a fourth voice of any of them.**
- **Do not put the practice into the register, the day-book, under a fifth head, or onto this county's copy of the hand paper, and do not have the copyist rule a head.** Nothing about the practice is on any paper in this volume.
- **Do not mend the separation by a declaration, do not print the word, do not put anything about the two of them in any document, do not let anybody else comment on it, and do not do this volume's relationship work.**
- **Do not fill or rule any head, put a finding under any of the ten questions, turn or time the half leaf, lift or schedule the bar at the Low Gate, lay or schedule the fourth course of stone, start the ninth yard of the wall, or pick the mallet up.**
- **Do not lift the cloth off the bench and do not have anybody ask what is under it.**
- **Do not cure the scar, do not say it is small, do not say it is going to close over, and do not cure or explain the bleed or give it a panel.**
- **Do not send anybody to the city four hundred miles off, do not reopen the shut road four hundred miles off, do not get the road that went quiet in Thawmonth YR 319 back, do not find the carter's mate, and do not trace who asked the fen county road office for the roll or who wrote the sentence on the folded sheet.**
- **Do not merge the three series, derive one from another, change the band figure, or print it anywhere. Do not convert a path's count into main-world days, and do not month, weekday or tide a path mouth.**
- **Do not call any of the four holes in the arrangement small, do not resolve any of them, do not renumber them and do not open a fifth.**
- **Do not thank anybody, in any chapter, in any speech, or in any state file this block writes.**
- **Do not print the kin-term, and do not print *stage*, *ledger*, *qualification*, *failed*, *charter*, *custodian*, *mechanism*, *small*, *volume* or *block*.** The word *failed* is not used about the shut road four hundred miles off and is not used about anything at all in this volume.
- **Do not produce, quote, mention or know about Ilyra Kest's route notes.** Those belong to Block 0003 and this block does not touch them.
- **Do not introduce a new final enemy. Do not move the ending. Do not write a marker of any kind.**
- **Do not repair the thirty-one pages of Volume 16 that carry withdrawn money figures.** They belong to closed blocks, `outline/volumes/volume-15-close.md` carries the same withdrawn set and is a closed record, and the deferral is recorded at `state/open-threads.md` 739, 751 and 752. **THE THIRTY, THE THIRTY-ONE AND THE FORTY ARE THREE COUNTS OF THREE SETS AND NOT THREE FIGURES THAT CORRECT ONE ANOTHER, and a successor may not print any of the three as a correction of another.**

## 7. The house prose, and the six mechanical rules that are not taste

**The voice is in Chapters 0810, 0807, 0805, 0804, 0803 and 0801.** Read them before you write a sentence and match them: short declaratives, a flat cadence, a great many plain negatives used inside a paragraph and never as the frame one is built on, the census sentence where who-understood is the point, and physical work, weather, distance and a man with a bad leg everywhere else. **The dateline line carries the weekday, the market, the state of the room over the weigh-house and about four more clauses.**

1. **Zero em dashes, zero en dashes, zero semicolons, zero exclamation marks, zero question marks, zero single asterisks and therefore no italics, zero straight double quotes and zero curly apostrophes.** Speech takes curly doubles. Apostrophes are straight. Per-line bold parity even on every line. Every file ends in a newline.
2. **One footed money column per chapter**: ten items, priced 1 to 41, a mark at forty-eight pence in every conversion, and the coda that names **some of** the figures in the chapter that are not in it, being that the list is a list of examples and not a complete inventory and a successor may not print it as complete.
3. **THE COLLISION SET MUST BE REBUILT OVER ALL EIGHT HUNDRED AND TEN FILES ON DISK, MUST NOT BE INHERITED, AND MUST BE EXPECTED TO COME BACK WITH NO FREE VALUE IN IT AT ALL.** The instrument is the printed total, taken as the spelled phrase in every spelling this manuscript prints across the whole hundred band, **and every spelling means the hundreds that value prints under and to no other, being *one hundred* and *a hundred* in the one hundreds, *two hundred* in the two hundreds and *three hundred* in the three hundreds, each with the remainder written as *and* the tens or as the tens with no *and*, plus the bare digit with a non-digit on either side of it, with a chapter heading not read as a total, run over every file whole.** **ON THE EIGHT HUNDRED AND TEN FILES THAT STAND NOW IT GIVES 284 PRINTED VALUES IN THE BAND SIXTY TO THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE BAND, AND ZERO FREE ONES, AND NOTHING UNDER SIXTY IS FREE EITHER, and that zero is true because the ten pages of Volume 16's Batch 0005 name 266, 273 and 326 in themselves, which is a different reason from the withdrawn one and may not be re-derived back into it.** **THE INSTRUMENT HAS TO BE WRITTEN OUT EVERY TIME AND IT HAS FAILED TWICE IN TWO OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and a writer who meets either withdrawn figure has to know which way it failed: too narrow, being an instrument that omits the *a hundred and …* spelling, returns values that are already printed, and that is how the withdrawn set of twelve came about, five of which are demonstrably printed; too wide, being an instrument that pairs every remainder with every hundred, counts *a hundred and sixty-six* as a printing of two hundred and sixty-six, and that is how the withdrawn figure of two hundred and eighty-four came about.** **AND THE CEILING OF THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE IS NOT LIFTED. Lifting it is an outline decision and `outline/volume-17.md` §7 has declined it on the page with three reasons and the third of them deciding, so this block's ten totals ARE REUSES AND THE HONEST THING TO DO IS WHAT ALL TEN OF VOLUME 16'S LAST BLOCK'S CLOSING PARAGRAPHS NOW DO: NAME THE REUSE ON THE PAGE AND GIVE THE REASON, WHICH IS ARITHMETIC**, in this form: the band from sixty to three hundred and forty-three has been searched whole again and three values in it are not a value any file in the manuscript before them has printed, being two hundred and sixty-six, two hundred and seventy-three and three hundred and twenty-six, and not one of the three can be used, because the over-figure of each of them is one of the barred six, and the ten totals of these ten columns are printed already, and the reason is arithmetic, and the route below sixty is shut, because ten distinct prices cannot sum under fifty-five and every total from fifty-five to fifty-nine is printed and nothing under that is free either. **The barred six are 14, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41 and none of them may be a price, an over-figure or a printed total anywhere.** Foot the column four ways and check the conversion separately from the sum. **THE FIGURES OF THIS BLOCK'S TEN TOTALS ARE THEN CHECKED AGAINST THE EIGHT-HUNDRED-AND-TEN-FILE SET AND NOT AGAINST A CARRIED ONE, and if the rebuild returns zero usable free values, which it will, that is a correct answer and must not be reprinted with a withdrawn reason.**
4. **`about` density, and the instrument is named because the band moves on it.** Volume 17 Batch 0001 runs **22.82 to 26.77** per 1,000 on a case-insensitive count of the token. **COUNT CASE-INSENSITIVELY AND WRITE TO 27.00, because the looser count is the one a successor can check and the stricter one cannot be brought under the line without breaking a sentence.** Aim for 22 to 27 and no page at or above 27.00. Keep the census sentence for the two or three beats in a chapter where who understood is the point and write the rest as action, weather, distance and silence. Do not write below 3,000 words and do not let a chapter run past about 4,300.
5. **THE CENSUS INSTRUMENT IS NAMED AT `state/continuity.md` 1708 AND A WRITER WHO QUOTES A FIGURE MUST NAME IT WITH IT.** Split the ten files on the blank line and count every non-empty paragraph. **Basis A is every paragraph except the title line. Basis B is Basis A less FOUR named groups in this block, because this block prints no System panel: the ten datelines, the dialogue paragraphs, the bold cost codas and the bold closing money columns.** A writer who quotes a Basis B figure must say in words which groups were taken out. The opener test is every paragraph beginning `No`, `Not`, `Never`, `None`, `Neither`, `Nobody`, `Nothing` or `No one`. **Volume 17 Batch 0001 is 0.0 and 0.0 and Volume 16's last three blocks are 0.0 and 0.0. THE SEVENTY-FIVE PER CENT CEILING IS NOT CROSSED IN THE LAST FIVE BLOCKS AND MUST NOT BE CROSSED IN THIS ONE.**
6. **Every count attached to a printed speech is footed off the printed words beside it**, and where a claim cannot be counted off the words printed next to it the claim is cut rather than left wrong. **A printed speech that has a word count beside it must have its words printed, and an unprinted speech must have no count.** Volume 16's three answers to the roll and Volume 17 Batch 0001's three answers may not be given a second time here, so any counted speech in this block is a new speech and it is footed by counting the words on the page and not by remembering them.

## 8. The running figures this block must keep

**Derive every one of these from the day number and never from a row, and print the figure at the chapter's OWN dateline.** `state/open-threads.md` item 721 is the finding that eight of Volume 16's Batch 0003 drove paragraphs carried a wrong calendar date because the chain was derived once and handed on, and the cheapest check is that Mudmonth is sixty days and every other month is thirty, so any day of month above thirty printed inside Mudmonth is wrong on sight, **and this block is entirely outside Mudmonth, being Goatmonth and Thawmonth only.**

- **The drove** goes up that lane on Thursdays and the count since the second of Mudmonth is floor((day - 2348) / 7) + 1 taken ON OR BEFORE the dateline. **It is 96 at day 3013 and 101 at day 3054, and it crosses a hundred at day 3041, which is a Thursday.** The drove paragraph's calendar date is the last Thursday on or before the dateline, **and a writer derives that date from the weekday and not from the count.** Nobody in nine counties has ever watched one go up.
- **The stone** has been carried two miles in one man's own hands since day 2347, elapsed and not inclusive. **It is 666 at day 3013 and 707 at day 3054.**
- **The scar** is counted from day 2580. **It is 433 days old at day 3013 and 474 at day 3054, and it is not cured and it is not going to close over.**
- **The ninth thing**, being the Wethergill end of a cart track, went quiet on the thirteenth of Hearthmonth YR 322, being day 2628, and nobody has been up that track since the second of Goatmonth, being day 2647. **Those two silence figures are counted from two different days and mixing them is the single most likely arithmetic defect in a chapter about that place: the last lime cart was 385 days ago at day 3013 and 426 at day 3054, and the road has been shut 366 days at day 3013 and 407 at day 3054.** Nobody goes up it in this block.
- **The practice mornings** are every day from 2611 to the dateline that is not a Thursday and not a Saturday. **The calendar count is 288 at day 3013 and 318 at day 3054, the count of mornings the practice was due on is 282 and 312, and the loss is six on every one of them.** The practice does not run on the five market mornings of this block's ten datelines and the page says so.
- **The number** said out loud at the fourth hour is **four**, it was eight until nine days of water, and it has not gone back, and two of the ten things came back after the water and two have not.
- **The printed notice** was read at the boards on day 2665, the first of Mudmonth was day 2706, it passed with nothing enforced, **and it is three hundred and seven days past its date at day 3013 and three hundred and forty-eight at day 3054 and has shut nothing.**
- **The roll** was nailed up on day 2827 and is **one hundred and eighty-six days on the boards at day 3013 and two hundred and twenty-seven at day 3054, with nine empty lines on each of three copies and the fourth line empty on all three.** **The sheet on the frame is a fifth thing and stays beside the roll and not over it, and its date is the twenty-ninth of Goatmonth YR 323, being day 3034, being five days off at day 3029 and two days past at day 3036 and twenty days past at day 3054.**
- **The two refusals** of Volume 15 are days 2509 and 2521, and neither man is asked anything.
- **The brood** stands at five frames under about nine straw skirts and no sixth has gone in, and the young man of about nineteen has said out loud three things in that street in about four and a half years and nobody has asked him for an account of them. **Nothing is on the page about the skirts that a character has to act on, and nobody has been asked whether his trade is on one of the nine lines of the hand paper.**
- **The standing broom** is about nine hundred yards of a line nine feet wide and the water laid nearly all of it flat, and it will not close over.
- **The wall's gap** is about nine feet long and four feet high and the ninth yard has not been started, and the mallet is on the bank two miles off with the line of stone and is not picked up. **Four separate things in this county are about nine feet across, being this gap, the width of the made road, the width of the standing broom and the length of that dead line of grass. Carry the noun with the number every time and never print the number on its own.**
- **The four lines of chalk** are on the stone sill of that weigh-house door **under the hood where the rain does not reach**, they mean four, nobody has read them out loud in about four and a half years, and the stick of chalk is in a press drawer and the man of about fifty-four has not asked for it.
- **The leaf at the back of that day-book carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody**, and the day-book stands at eleven entries and the register holds ten questions with no finding under any of them.
- **The bleed** began on the fifth of Wolfmonth YR 323, being day 2920, and is **ninety-three days old at day 3013 and one hundred and thirty-four at day 3054, and it has not faded and nobody in nine counties knows about it and it is in no document and it gets no panel.**
- **The hand lamp** goes on the coping at the low side of that causeway four days south every Monday afternoon in the winter, and **two of this block's ten datelines are Mondays, being 3045 and 3052, so a writer may put the lamp there on either of those two afternoons and may not put it there on any of the other eight, and the page says the afternoon is the lamp's if it says it at all.**
- **The firsts of a month** are twenty-fifth at day 3036 and that one carries Chapter 0814, **and the count is not begun again.**
